short: Strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced the abdication of Tsar Nicholas II, ending the Russian Empire.
full:
On 8 March 1917 (23 February in the Julian calendar), mass protests broke out in Petrograd over food shortages and war exhaustion. When troops ordered to suppress the demonstrations mutinied and joined the crowds, the imperial government lost control of the capital. Within days, Tsar Nicholas II abdicated, ending over three centuries of Romanov rule.

Power devolved to a fragile dual arrangement between the moderate Provisional Government and the radical Petrograd Soviet. The Provisional Government fatally chose to continue the war effort despite sweeping demoralization, setting the stage for further upheaval and the eventual Bolshevik seizure of power later that year.
